profile.reading: This building is the second of two structures making up SFO1, part of Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster at 2401 and 2403 Walsh Avenue in Santa Clara, California, mapped as a separate OpenStreetMap way from its immediate neighbor at essentially the same address. Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name of a data center real estate company with a documented and unusually well-sourced corporate history. These Silicon Valley facilities trace back to CenturyLink Savvis-heritage colocation assets, which were divested and became Evoque Data Center Solutions around 2020 to 2021 under Brookfield-affiliated ownership, later rebranded Centersquare, and rebranded again to Csquare ahead of its July 16, 2026 initial public offering. That IPO priced at 21 dollars per share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, and Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. Per Csquare own SEC registration prospectus, the company overall portfolio as of March 31, 2026 spanned 64 sites across 21 major metro markets in the US, Canada, and the UK, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, with CEO Spencer Mullee and CFO Steven Cook both having joined from the company Evoque-era leadership. The same prospectus Properties table lists two Silicon Valley buildings under the SFO1 code, designated SFO1_A at 60,982 rentable square feet, 64.9 percent occupied, and SFO1_B at 38,634 rentable square feet, 63.9 percent occupied, both company-owned, though which specific street address corresponds to which suffix could not be confirmed this session, so no single building-level square footage figure is assigned to this record individually.

reading.body:
The Csquare SFO1 campus in Santa Clara spans two buildings with a combined 129.4 megawatts of utility power. This places it outside California's top ten published data center campuses by capacity, though only eleven facilities statewide publish power figures at all, and the state total of 365 megawatts across mapped sites suggests most capacity remains undisclosed. At an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack for AI training density, 129.4 megawatts of total utility power would support roughly 3,200 racks, though total IT load is not published and utility power includes cooling, power conversion, and other non-compute infrastructure.

The campus holds SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and PCI DSS certifications, qualifying it for regulated enterprise and financial workloads. LEED certification indicates energy management infrastructure. No AI-specific certification, power delivery timeline, or customer list is published. Csquare's prospectus lists the two buildings as separately occupied and company-owned but does not assign individual power figures to either structure.

SFO1 is one of two buildings OpenStreetMap contributors have mapped at this address and one component of a larger Csquare Silicon Valley cluster spanning SFO1 through SFO4. Csquare overall operates 64 sites with roughly 389 megawatts of sellable capacity across North America and the UK, making this campus a fraction of portfolio scale. The operator is a publicly traded Brookfield-controlled company as of July 2026. No information is published on available power for new tenants, power delivery timelines, or current tenant mix.
